question: Which legal system in Britain lets an old statute lapse through long disuse, with no formal repeal?
answer: Scotland. Scots law, drawing on Roman civil law, holds that an old Act can fall into desuetude: long neglect plus a settled contrary practice ends its force. English law has none, which is why in 1818 an English court had to grant a defendant's demand for trial by combat; Parliament abolished it in 1819.
move: Whether silence can kill a rule depends on whose rulebook it is.
trap: Believing every law stands until formally repealed, as English law holds.
reference: Brown v Magistrates of Edinburgh, 1931 SLT 456, Court of Session, 1931
